proposition: Ibn Turka acted as patron and broker for a younger protégé, Sharaf al-Dīn Yaʿqūb, whom he recommended by letter to an amir (4), to Iskandar's vizier (12) and, in letter 6, asked another amir (Niẓām al-Dīn Aḥmad Ṣāʿidī) to look into the situation of; MK identifies him with the Sayyid Sharaf al-Dīn Yaʿqūb who became qadi of Yazd after his teacher's departure.

mediation.who: Ibn Turka, writing to Fīrūzshāh, Ḥāfiẓ Rāzī, Niẓām al-Dīn Aḥmad
mediation.note: Letters to third parties ask or offer favours; the text survives only in copies made after his lifetime (except the marginal letters in MS Majlis 10196).

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
